findings.issue: The dead-leader cleanup fix depends on the caller first polling/reaping the exited parent. interrupt() calls _owned_group_exists before process.poll(). An exited unreaped parent is a zombie with no environment token, causing group validation to reject the whole owned group. Its live child is never signalled, while finally at lines118-120 removes the ownership record. Independent two-case reproduction: reap_first=True cleaned child; reap_first=False raised UnownedProcess for owned group54384, child remained stateS and owned_names became(). Reviewer cleaned all test processes. The added regression manually calls leader.process.wait(), masking the natural crash path.
findings.suggestion: Root diagnosis required after this bounded re-review: reap the known child before initial group census, distinguish dead/zombie/missing census members from live ownership failures, and retain ownership when termination cannot be verified. Reproduce natural leader exit without externally waiting/polling first; preserve unrelated sentinel and wrong-token refusal. Do not run another identical worker review loop.
